verdict: Research arc on 2,511 metabolic enzymes, and the process is the point. I expected the paralog-buffering law (essential = no isoenzyme backup). My first redundancy proxy — genes sharing a REACTION — REFUTED it, even reversing the sign (essential enzymes shared reactions with MORE genes, +0.17). But that proxy was CONFOUNDED (it counts obligate complex co-members as 'backups'), so I fetched UniProt sequence FAMILIES and measured true isoenzyme paralogs — and buffering came back clean and correct: essential enzymes have far FEWER same-family paralogs (median 0 vs 2, effect -0.30, p=2e-14). So the honest finding is TWO independent axes of metabolic essentiality: (1) CENTRALITY — the dominant one — embedded in a complex (effect +0.50), spanning many pathways (+0.48), a PPI hub (+0.42), and a SPECIALIST (fewer reactions, -0.31); and (2) PARALOG BUFFERING — real and orthogonal — lacking a sequence-family backup, which still adds +0.021 AUC on top of centrality alone. Together held-out AUC 0.862 vs a label-shuffled null 0.514: an enzyme is indispensable when it sits at a central junction AND has no twin to cover for it. This is the near-field structure/network layer that IS recoverable, and the run is a live example of the session's core discipline — a confounded proxy gave a confident WRONG answer until a cleaner measurement corrected it. HONEST LIMITS: UniProt family granularity varies (broad superfamilies dilute paralog counts); centrality's sub-features are correlated (one latent axis); LOEUF/dep_frac are both importance measures; and this explains WHICH enzymes are essential, not the downstream phenotype of removing one (that stays measurement's job).
